en: Emilio Aguinaldo declared Philippine independence on June 12, 1898, ending 333 years of Spanish colonial rule that began in 1565.
The Philippine eagle, our national bird, has a massive wingspan measuring up to two meters, making it one of the largest eagles globally.
The Philippine Supreme Court consists of exactly one Chief Justice and fourteen Associate Justices, totaling fifteen members in the highest judicial branch.
While the Philippines has over 180 distinct languages, the 1987 Constitution officially recognizes only Filipino and English as the two national languages.
In the Giant Lantern Festival, competing lanterns in San Fernando City can reach 20 feet in diameter and use over 6,000 light bulbs.
The Igorot indigenous groups inhabit the Cordillera Administrative Region, which covers roughly 19,400 square kilometers across six mountain provinces.
National hero Jose Rizal was only 35 years old when executed in 1896, having already written two famous novels before turning thirty.
After a 2016 scientific survey, the official count of Philippine islands increased from 7,107 to 7,641 due to better mapping technology.
Filipino scientist Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first female student admitted to Harvard Medical School in 1935, a decade before official acceptance.
The Philippine Senate has exactly 24 elected senators, which is 12 fewer than the 36 senators in the United States Senate.
The Philippine national flag has a length-to-width ratio of 2:1, meaning it is exactly twice as long as it is wide.
The University of Santo Tomas was founded in 1611, making it exactly 25 years older than Harvard University in the United States.
